Large language models (LLMs) can not only store and retrieve commonsense knowledge effectively , but also exhibit the ability to make inferences based on their stored knowledge in commonsense reasoning tasks .
outputs: Generated reasoning paths and answers to commonsense questions
The outputs include generated reasoning paths, knowledge triplets, and answers to multiple-choice questions.

quote: We propose ReComSBench, a framework that improves existing benchmarks by making hidden reasoning attributes explicit. It introduces three novel metrics for decoupled evaluations of commonsense knowledge and reasoning capabilities.

...Metric 2: Marginal Sampling Gain... evaluates the overall sampling performance of the model... Metric 3: Knowledge Coverage Ratio... evaluate single-path reasoning quality... Knowledge Balanced Accuracy... explicitly prompts the model with the knowledge required for the answer...

We introduce three novel metrics: Knowledge Balanced Accuracy for assessing commonsense knowledge, and Marginal Sampling Gain and Knowledge Coverage Ratio for evaluating overall domain reasoning and single inference quality.
